chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

When it is Friday, and the people of Paradise are in Paradise while the people of Hell are in the Fire, the inhabitants of Paradise will know that it is Friday due to what they witness of enhanced pleasure and joy, and the denizens of Hell will know that it is Friday because the wardens of Hell seize them.
ai.seo_question: How do the inhabitants of Paradise and Hell recognize the day of Friday?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this narration highlights the cosmic significance of Jumu'ah as a day of amplified emotional states for both realms, reflecting the Shia emphasis on Friday as a pivotal temporal marker in eschatology. The contrast between the spiritual ecstasy of the blessed and the visceral dread of the damned underscores the day's role in manifesting divine justice and mercy, a theme often explored in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the 'best of days'.
